guideTitle: 7 Best Folding Portable Wheelchair Ramps in 2026
metaDescription: Seven folding wheelchair ramps from 3 ft to 8 ft compared on folded size, weight, rise range and edge protection, with the slope math to size one correctly.
introParagraphs: A folding wheelchair ramp earns its place by shrinking. Most of the picks below close in half like a suitcase, so a ramp that is 36 to 96 inches long in use becomes a flat slab 36 to 48 inches long and about 14 inches wide. That is the difference between a ramp that stays in a hallway closet and one you can actually bring to a relative's porch.

Folding adds a hinge, and the hinge adds a few things to check: a seam in the deck, a latch to hold the halves together and a carry handle that has to take the full weight. The ramp's length still decides slope. A 3 ft ramp over a 9 inch step climbs at 1 in 4, while a 6 ft ramp over 6 inches climbs at 1 in 12, and the longest listed here, at 8 ft, reaches 24 inches at that steeper angle.

We evaluated each pick from its product page, stated dimensions and buyer feedback. These are portable aids and not code-compliant permanent entrances, and a therapist can help match slope to a specific chair or scooter.

products.name: HYUNAN METHOD 3FT Portable Wheelchair Ramp
products.description:
The Hyunan Method 3FT is a folding aluminum ramp that weighs 14.02 lb and carries an 800 lb capacity. It opens to 36 by 29 by 2.4 inches and folds to 36 by 14.5 by 3.2 inches, with guardrails and reflective strips included. The stated rise range is 3 to 9 inches.

The weakness of any 36 inch ramp is steepness. A 3 inch step gives a comfortable 1 in 12, but a 9 inch step climbs at 1 in 4, which is a lot for a manual chair. The listing recommends moving to a longer ramp when in doubt, which is the right call, and it does not describe the surface material in the text we reviewed.

In ownership, 14.02 lb can be carried one-handed, and the folded slab slides behind a seat or under a bed. It weighs less than the 4 ft Hyunan Method at 18.43 lb and has a smaller footprint. It is the best choice here for one or two low steps and for people who prioritize lifting ease over reach.
products.bestFor: One or two low steps for someone who needs the lightest full-size ramp.

Listing advises sizing up when in doubt

products.name: HYUNAN METHOD 4FT Portable Wheelchair Ramp
products.description:
The 4FT Hyunan Method steps up in length while keeping the same layout as its 3 ft sibling. It measures 48 by 29 by 2.4 inches open, folds to 48 by 14.5 by 3.2 inches and weighs 18.43 lb. The 800 lb rating and the guardrails with reflective strips carry over.

An extra foot of run helps the slope. A 6 inch step gives about 1 in 8 on this ramp, versus 1 in 6 on the 3 footer. The 12 inch top of the range is still a steep 1 in 4, and the guardrails reduce the usable lane a little, so check wide tires.

In ownership, the added 4.4 lb over the 3 ft model is a modest price for the gentler angle. It stores in a trunk without trouble. Compared with the VNN 6 ft, it is easier to lift but cannot reach as tall a step comfortably. It is a good middle choice when you want a moderate rise range and a documented spec sheet.
products.bestFor: Steps of 4 to 8 inches where a documented, mid-length folding ramp is wanted.
pros: Gentler slope than the 3 ft sibling at 6 inches
Full open and folded dimensions published
Lists 800 lb with rails and reflective strips
Fits into a car trunk without trouble
cons: Rails narrow the usable lane slightly
Heavier than the 3 ft Hyunan by about 4 lb

products.name: FACHNUO 3FT Portable Wheelchair Ramp
products.description:
The Fachnuo 3FT uses pleated aluminum to add friction under wheels and fits baffles on both sides to keep tires in line. Reflective strips help the ramp stand out in low light. It opens to 36 by 29 by 2 inches and folds to 36 by 14.5 by 3.2 inches, and the rated rise is 3 to 9 inches.

The listing does not state a weight or a load rating in the text we reviewed, which is the biggest gap against the Hyunan 3 ft with its 14.02 lb and 800 lb. The top of the range is steep at 3 feet, and the ramp is close in design to several others, so there is little to set it apart apart from the baffles.

In ownership, the pleated surface gives a firm footing for walkers and the baffles help a nervous driver. The folded slab is easy to slide into a closet. Compared with the Kolotool 3 ft, it offers more edge protection but fewer stated numbers. Ask the seller for the weight and rating before you buy.
products.bestFor: Walker and chair users who value side baffles and a pleated, grippy deck.

Baffles on both sides keep wheels in line

Little to separate it from near twin ramps

products.name: KOLOTOOL Portable Wheelchair Ramps 3FT
products.description:
The Kolotool 3FT is a folding, non-skid aluminum ramp aimed at one or two steps between 3 and 9 inches. The page states an 800 lb capacity and describes high-strength aluminum alloy. It folds in half for transport and storage and is also marketed for travel.

Because it is only 36 inches long, steepness is the main caution. Anything above about 4 inches becomes demanding, and at 9 inches the slope is 1 in 4. That makes independent use tough and suggests a helper for most wheelchair users. The listing gives no weight in the text we reviewed.

In ownership, the compact folded form tucks away in a closet or a car footwell. Compared with the Fachnuo 3 ft, it is clearer about its rating, while the Fachnuo is clearer about edge protection. It suits a buyer who wants a quick stand-by ramp for a visit and plans to use it at the low end of its range.
products.bestFor: A stand-by ramp for visits to homes with a single low step.

products.name: VNN Portable Wheelchair Ramp 6FT Seamless
products.description:
The VNN 6FT puts the fold at the center and makes it seamless, so the deck feels more continuous when you roll across the middle. The listing says this lowers the chance of tripping and reduces the strain of crossing a hinge line. A folded-and-coated aluminum surface adds friction, and it is listed for steps of 6 to 18 inches.

Six feet equals 72 inches of run, so a 6 inch step gives a gentle 1 in 12 slope. The top of the range, 18 inches, climbs at 1 in 4. The warning not to exceed the maximum weight capacity appears on the page, but a number is not given in the text we reviewed, so ask before you rely on it.

In ownership, the folded length is half of 72 inches, which fits a larger trunk or a van. It is a clear step up in reach from the Hyunan 4 ft and avoids the support legs and setup of the 8 ft models. It suits a porch with a moderate rise where a 4 ft ramp would feel too steep.
products.bestFor: Porch steps of 6 to 12 inches where the middle seam should not jolt small casters.
pros: Seamless center hinge smooths the middle of the deck
Covers steps of 6 to 18 inches
Folded plus coated aluminum surface adds grip
Folds without tools for carrying
cons: Slope at the 18 inch end is steep
Capacity number is missing from the text

products.name: TaiH Leo 8FT Wheelchair Ramp With Support Legs
products.description:
The TaiH Leo is a folding 8 ft ramp that opens to 96 by 29 inches and closes to 48 by 14 inches. Two adjustable legs brace the long span, and transition plates sit at the top and bottom edges. It is listed for rises of 8 to 24 inches, which covers a short porch, a van sill or two high steps.

With 96 inches of run, an 8 inch rise comes out at 1 in 12, and a 24 inch rise at 1 in 4. The legs add a little work, because you need level ground under each one, but they keep the long span from flexing. Setup is described as tool-free and quick.

In ownership, the folded size matches a 4 ft ramp, so it is easier to move than its 96 inch open length suggests. Compared with the Fachnuo 8 ft, it names its plates and legs more clearly in the listing. It suits a household with a recurring tall step and a trunk or van to carry it.
products.bestFor: A porch or van entry with an 8 to 16 inch rise that needs a braced span.
pros: Adjustable legs brace the long 96 inch span
Plates at both ends smooth entry and exit
Closes to 48 by 14 inches for carrying
Tool-free setup is described as quick
cons: Legs must sit on level ground at each use
Slope at 24 inches is still steep

products.name: FACHNUO 8FT Portable Wheelchair Ramp With Support Legs
products.description:
The Fachnuo 8FT is a close sibling of the TaiH Leo with the same 96 inch open length and 8 to 24 inch rise range. It adds baffles and reflective strips to both sides and uses support legs to hold the span. Folded, it measures 48 by 14.5 by 6.3 inches, which is thicker than the 4 ft folding ramps.

The pleated, non-slip aluminum surface is meant for traction in a range of weather. As with every 8 ft ramp, the slope at the top of the range is 1 in 4, so the lower half of the rise range is where it works best. Listing text we reviewed gives no weight or capacity, which makes a question to the seller worthwhile.

In ownership, the 6.3 inch folded depth takes more space than the 3 inch slabs, but it still fits a trunk. Compared with the TaiH Leo, it is more explicit about edge protection and less explicit about plates. It is a reasonable pick when you want baffles on a long ramp.
products.bestFor: Taller entries where side baffles and reflective strips are a priority.

buyingCriteria.explanation: A folding ramp is chosen as much for how it stores as how it climbs. The Hyunan 3 ft weighs 14.02 lb and folds to 36 by 14.5 by 3.2 inches, the Hyunan 4 ft weighs 18.43 lb at 48 inches long, and the 8 ft models fold to 48 inches but are thicker at 6.3 inches on the Fachnuo. Measure the trunk or closet and think about who lifts. A ramp you cannot lift will not be used.

The fold line is the weakest point on any bi-fold ramp, and a raised seam can catch small front casters. The VNN 6 ft uses a seamless center hinge, while the others use standard fold lines. Inspect latches and pins for firmness. A ramp that flexes or rattles at the fold should be avoided.

Each folding ramp lists a rise range, but the top of that range is steep. The 3 ft models climb at 1 in 4 at 9 inches, the VNN 6 ft at 1 in 4 at 18 inches and the 8 ft models at 1 in 4 at 24 inches. Aim for the lower half of the range. When your step sits between sizes, choose the longer ramp.

Capacity should cover the user, the device and anything carried. The Hyunan 3 ft and 4 ft and the Kolotool list 800 lb, while the Fachnuo 3 ft and 8 ft and the VNN 6 ft give no figure in the text we reviewed. Listings that skip these numbers deserve a question to the seller. Treat any rating as a maximum.

Baffles, guardrails and plates guide wheels and soften the entry. The Fachnuo ramps use baffles and reflective strips, the Hyunan ramps use guardrails with reflective strips and the TaiH Leo adds plates at both ends. Side rails help a nervous driver, but they narrow the lane. Check against your tire width.

Long ramps need support, and the TaiH Leo and Fachnuo 8 ft use adjustable legs. Legs prevent sag but demand level ground, so check the landing at your door. Short ramps without legs rely on the deck alone. Test any ramp for rocking before use.

howWeEvaluated.title: Portability
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared stated weights and folded sizes. The Hyunan 3 ft at 14.02 lb is the lightest, the Hyunan 4 ft at 18.43 lb is next and the 8 ft models are bulkier. Folded depth mattered too, with the Fachnuo 8 ft at 6.3 inches the thickest.

howWeEvaluated.title: Fold and hinge design
howWeEvaluated.description: We read what each page says about the hinge and the carrying method. The VNN 6 ft stands out for a seamless center hinge. The rest use standard folds, and we docked pages that give no detail on latches.

howWeEvaluated.title: Slope and rise range
howWeEvaluated.description: We computed slope from stated length and rise. The VNN 6 ft and the 8 ft ramps give 1 in 12 at the bottom of their ranges, while the 3 ft models are steeper at any given rise. Pages that overstate the top of the range lost credit.

howWeEvaluated.title: Edges and traction
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at baffles, guardrails, plates and surface textures. The Fachnuo ramps and the Hyunan ramps lead with side protection, and the TaiH Leo adds plates. This is based on product specs and buyer feedback, not measured friction.

howWeEvaluated.title: Spec transparency
howWeEvaluated.description: We gave credit for stated weight and capacity. The Hyunan pair and the Kolotool publish an 800 lb rating, while the Fachnuo and VNN pages leave capacity out of the text we reviewed.

faq.q: How does a folding ramp differ from a solid one?
faq.a: A folding ramp has a center hinge so it closes into a flat slab that is easy to carry and store. The hinge adds a seam in the deck and a latch to check. A seamless hinge, like the VNN 6 ft, reduces the bump.
The Hyunan Method 3 ft lists 14.02 lb, and the 4 ft model lists 18.43 lb. The other listings give no weight in the text we reviewed. Ask the seller if lifting is a concern.

faq.q: What length do I need for a 6 inch step?
faq.a: A 6 ft ramp gives about 1 in 12 over 6 inches, a 4 ft gives about 1 in 8 and a 3 ft gives 1 in 6. The shorter options are steeper to push. Choose the longest that fits your storage.

faq.q: Do all folding ramps need support legs?
faq.a: No. The 3 ft, 4 ft and 6 ft models here rely on the deck alone. The TaiH Leo and Fachnuo 8 ft add legs to brace a long span. Legs need level ground.
They help guide tires and add visibility, as on the Hyunan and Fachnuo ramps, but they narrow the usable lane. If your chair is wide, check the clear width between rails. Narrow chairs benefit most.

faq.q: Can I use a folding ramp in the rain?
faq.a: Textured aluminum helps, and the VNN and Fachnuo ramps use folded or pleated surfaces. Keep the deck clear of leaves and wipe it dry. Avoid use on ice or in heavy snow.

faq.q: Is a folding ramp good for a permanent entrance?
faq.a: It is meant for temporary or occasional use. A permanent entrance may need landings, handrails and a permit depending on your area. A therapist or local professional can advise.
